PRISM setup: selecting and scanning the incident energy
Ge(880) is the baseline candidate for the Ag K-edge at 25.5 keV.
Crystal rotation and motorized axes preserve the focused spot during the scan.
The same CZT measures If and I0 in separate motorized configurations.
SHADOW4 + GEANT4 optimize flux, bandwidth and background.

Source: FINAL/Progetto.pdf, methodology pp. 3–7. Ge(880) is a baseline candidate, not a frozen design. I0: sample removed, CZT repositioned into the attenuated direct beam; calibrated attenuation and linear-rate operation. Drawing is conceptual and not to scale. Design freeze M6. Incident bandwidth target ≤10 eV FWHM is distinct from detector energy resolution.
VOXES provides the experimental starting point
Manti, Simone, et al. "Enhancing Performances of the VOXES Bragg Spectrometer for XES Investigations."

Existing VOXES results shown here were acquired in X-ray emission configurations. They establish controlled crystal rotation and focusing, not demonstrated fluorescence XAS. Commissioning target M18: count rates within 20%, spot size and incident-energy resolution within 10% of simulation predictions. Source: FINAL/Progetto.pdf, pp. 4, 7–8; existing slide references.
A custom CZT array for hard-X-ray fluorescence
Distribute the rate and monitor each pixel
Gain, charge sharing, pile-up and stability

Design baseline and acquisition specifications: FINAL/Progetto.pdf, pp. 4–5. Efficiency plot is a comparative detector absorption calculation, not a measured qualification result. CZT fabrication and characterization remain project activities.
Methods to validate on the PRISM multichannel CZT
Manti, S. et al. Pulse-Shape Discrimination with Machine Learning for CZT Detectors at DAΦNE Beam Test Facility. Condens. Matter 2026, 11, 38
Manti, S., et al. "Machine-learning-enhanced event selection for BEGe detectors in the VIP experiment." Journal of Instrumentation 21.01 (2026): P01036.

The plotted pulse-selection example is prior detector-analysis experience (BEGe/VIP context), not proof that the PRISM CZT already meets its targets. CZT and BEGe references are retained from the original presentation. Qualify efficiency, energy response, gain equalization, linearity, rate dependence, dead time, pile-up and channel uniformity on the multichannel detector. Targets: FINAL/Progetto.pdf, ER2 and MS2. The ≤2% detector resolution at Ag Kα must not be confused with the ≤10 eV incident-beam bandwidth.
Ag K-edge XANES: the quantitative demonstration
Extract Ag Kα, correct background and live time, then normalize to I0.

Source: FINAL/Progetto.pdf, O3/ER3, methodology and WP4/MS4. Ag K-edge ≈25.5 keV; fluorescence Ag Kα ≈22.2 keV. Compare metallic foil and two Ag(I) compounds with different coordination. These are planned measurements, not existing PRISM spectra. In the thin/dilute limit, corrected If/I0 is proportional to absorption. For thick/concentrated samples assess self-absorption explicitly. Quantify acquisition time and accessible operating domain; do not claim an unvalidated one-hour performance. Reference dataset M21, realistic-sample demonstration M24.
From instrument design to the Ag demonstration

Timeline and milestones: FINAL/Progetto.pdf pp. 7–8. WP1 M1–6, WP2 M4–15, WP3 M10–18, WP4 M16–24. Reference-compound dataset D3 M21, realistic-sample dataset D4 M24. Original Gantt retained. The oral narrative follows scientific concepts; the timeline summarizes delivery.
Crystal optics, ray tracing and integration

Team and FTE verified in FINAL/Progetto.pdf p.7, collaborations pp.9–10. Total 1.7 FTE. Industrial letters of support indicate interest, not guaranteed delivery or co-funding. Transfer to EuAPS follows laboratory validation.
Source: FINAL/Progetto.pdf, Costs, and FINAL/Costs.pdf. Requested total €112k: €69k in 2027 and €43k in 2028. Estimated in-kind €45k is separate. The original itemized cost table is retained.
Use the existing Si PIN for preliminary tests
Optimize acceptance, scan steps and dwell

Mitigations from FINAL/Progetto.pdf, Risk Assessment. The existing Si PIN is a reduced-efficiency commissioning fallback, not an equivalent replacement for the final CZT demonstration. No numerical risk-priority score is claimed.
PRISM: a validated laboratory fluorescence-XAS platform
A commissioned instrument supported by source-to-detector simulations.
A calibrated detector, waveform readout and validated reconstruction methods.
Ag K-edge XANES as the validation benchmark
Quantitative reference data and a defined operating domain for realistic samples.

Expected outputs and impact, not achieved results: FINAL/Progetto.pdf, objectives, deliverables and impact sections. Emphasize reusable detector/readout, validated simulations and analysis procedures. Laboratory validation establishes the basis for long measurement campaigns and future transfer.

enables studies of materials under operating conditions.
